chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When the slave becomes blind, he has been freed."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave who becomes blind?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'itq al-'ism' (emancipation due to a defect), where blindness serves as an automatic trigger for a slave's freedom. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the intrinsic value of human dignity and the master's obligation to compensate for the loss of the slave's utility, reflecting a compassionate approach to manumission found in the works of scholars like Al-Tusi.
